items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: I got worried about him leaving the band through Chester Clark, who was the trumpet player with Trent, wonderful trumpet player, tremendous. He said, you should wire Troy Floyd because he'll need a man in that seat and he'll fit it.

ctx.x: Well, tell me a little bit more about Troy Floyd's band. I don't know too much about it, it's what you've told me.

Well, the history of Troy Floyd's band goes way back to the days of Alfonso Trent, who was a band that was organized with Texas musicians and Arkansas, because Trent originally was from a little town of Fort Smith, Arkansas. His estate was still there, I visited the estate just a couple of three years ago. And Trent was playing at the Adolphus Hotel, incidentally the first name of a band to be put into one of these big establishments. So Troy had his band organized with mostly Texas men. And the great trumpet…
Well, how did he play then? Did he use many head arrangements? Would he just be faking all the time or what? I don't know.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: I got to talking to some of the guys in his band and also Trent's band. So Chester Clark... said, why don't you try to get that job with Troy's band?

ctx.x: Oh, yes. I knew him. Very much in Chicago.

That's right. Well, Lee was playing in the same neighborhood. And that's when Troy Floyd came to town. And I was a fellow who always liked to follow musicians. And I happened to go to a party I was having there for Troy. Troy was a great man then. And I got to talking to some of the guys in his band and also Trent's band. So Chester Clark, which is another great trumpet player, said, why don't you try to get that job with Troy's band? He says, Claude Kennedy's leaving. Oh, I says, I don't know if I could play…
After having that self-edged training for a year and a half, that comes to see for you.
